name: Tomas Torres

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I work with the Work Futures Panel, independent of AI firms, employers, unions, political parties and government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What happens on your shift?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead the morning service team for home internet accounts. When a bill and an outage report disagree, I follow the dates until I can tell the customer what really happened. I have a two-year college diploma and am one of the best at these disputes, though the lead wage is ordinary for this job. I use our approved AI assistant every day to search old cases, then check the raw service log.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What does the home budget look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Salma stocks shelves at a pharmacy. Our children are seven and eleven, and the mortgage comes out of both wages. We have five months of expenses saved and a few other centres nearby. I try new tools early, but I want to know what the new button did before I tell an agent to trust it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team the assistant saves us searching time, but it cannot turn an outage into a customer’s unpaid bill. The service log still settles outage-credit disputes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think the lead job and our household pay would hold. Five months saved gives us room, although the mortgage and school costs keep it from being holiday money.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep taking disputed outage calls and show agents how I check the service log against an AI summary. In the first year I will put part of each pay toward a six-month reserve before replacing the living-room sofa.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the job. A slower technology year would let us fix our ordinary budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What error have you caught?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The assistant once used a neighbourhood outage notice for a different street. I checked the address and prevented a wrong credit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why wait on the sofa?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The old one is worn but usable. The extra month in the reserve would pay bills if one of us lost shifts.

say: I would welcome **faster searches** with a service-log check.
I would keep **outage credits** tied to the right address.
think: I expect my **lead job** and our two household wages to hold through these small shortcuts.
I treat five months saved as **mortgage protection**.
do: Keep resolving **outage disputes** and show newer agents how to check AI summaries against service logs.
Save toward **six months** and delay replacing the usable sofa until then.
feel: **Calm** about work and able to save.
S0.quote: The service log still settles outage-credit disputes.
fieldNote: He uses **approved AI daily** but checks source records.
His **five-month reserve** gives breathing room, not unlimited spending.
A worn **sofa** is a delayable purchase.

steps.text: Keep resolving outage disputes and checking AI summaries against service logs
Save from each pay toward six months of expenses before buying a sofa
Delay replacing the usable sofa until six months of expenses are saved

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the floor to measure repeat outage calls after automatic replies. If the easy questions go, the remaining agents need fair targets for the messy bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can learn the new review system, but fewer routine calls could mean fewer paid shifts. Salma’s pharmacy wage helps; it would not cover our mortgage alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I will test the new AI review view on forty closed outage cases with our quality lead during paid shifts. I will show the repeat-call count to management and ask for a paid correction block. If my rota falls in the first year, I will apply for posted paid quality roles at nearby centres only if written wages and hours cover the mortgage and fit school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am anxious about hours rather than learning. Being good with the screen does not guarantee a full rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a quality title anywhere?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. Salma and I would compare the weekly hours, the bus fare and the children’s pickup before I accept an offer. A better hourly rate can leave less after travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you learn from the test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I want to see which outage notices the new screen treats as current. I would write down each stale source, not just whether the answer sounded smooth.

say: I would count **repeat outage calls** after automatic replies.
I would ask for **paid correction time** backed by the count.
think: I can learn **AI review** quickly because I already inspect the raw outage logs each day.
I fear **lost paid shifts** despite strong dispute skills.
do: Test **forty closed outages** on the new AI review view during paid shifts.
Ask management for **paid correction blocks** using repeat-call counts.
Apply after cuts for **posted paid quality** with written net mortgage-covering wages, hours and pickup.
S1.quote: A better hourly rate can leave less after travel.
fieldNote: His AI test is **new learning**, not unchanged daily use.
He takes counts to management **himself**, without claiming collective bargaining.
Travel fare and school pickup affect **usable pay**.

steps.text: Learn AI review view on forty closed outages during paid shifts
Apply after cuts for posted quality work with written net mortgage-covering wages, hours and pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say full thinking AI by 2028 could answer nearly every home internet chat. Robots around 2031 do not delay the risk to our screen work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect our centre to cut many agents, perhaps my lead post too. Five months saved buys a search, but two children and a mortgage can outlast that cushion.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will ask for written staffing dates and pause the sofa purchase. I will compare actual paid service-audit vacancies, including travel costs, without leaving my current wage. If my post ends in the first year after 2028, I will move only on a written paid offer whose wages and hours cover our mortgage after travel and fit school pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed, even with five months saved. Nearby contact centres could all cut roles while I am still looking for paid work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you do service audits?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know the outage logs, but audit work has rules I have not used. I would complete a required audit course if a posted paid vacancy funds its fees and pays my learning hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Salma?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show Salma the written dates, not a rumour from the floor. We would check her pharmacy rota before I accept anything farther away.

say: I would warn **2028 AGI** could answer most chats.
I would separate **2031 robots** from the screen deadline.
think: I expect **centre cuts**, possibly my lead post.
I know five months saved cannot carry our **mortgage and children** through a long local job search.
do: Request **written staffing dates** and defer the sofa.
Complete **funded required audit training** on paid time only for a posted paid vacancy.
Move after job loss only on a **written offer** with travel-adjusted mortgage-covering wages/hours and pickup, after checking Salma’s pharmacy rota.
S2.quote: Nearby contact centres could all cut roles while I am still looking for paid work.
fieldNote: He treats **audit vacancies** as real only when posted.
The **course gate** includes funded fees and paid learning hours.
Salma’s **pharmacy rota** affects a farther commute.

steps.text: Delay buying the sofa while keeping the current one usable
Complete required audit course only for posted paid vacancy funding fees and learning hours
Move after job loss on written net mortgage-covering wages/hours fitting pickup after checking Salma’s rota

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell agents the extra years let us inspect real audit posts before the calls go. General AI reaches our chats in 2031, and hands-on robots follow around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could learn the audit rules while still earning the lead wage, but a screen job may not last forever under AGI. I want a paid bridge rather than a shiny title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep the outage desk and ask for a paid shadow day in service audit if the employer posts a place. If a posted paid audit role offers written wages and hours covering our mortgage after travel and school pickup, and funds its required course on paid time, I will complete it. In the first year after 2031 I will move only on a written offer meeting those terms after Salma and I compare both rotas.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious but able to prepare. Five years lets me meet the person doing the job, not just read the vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask the auditor?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask how often an outage credit is overturned and who signs the final account. If the shadow day is unpaid, I cannot treat it as a trial of income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no audit post opens?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep the lead shift while it pays and check other centres twice a year. I will not buy a course for a role that has not been posted.

say: I would ask for **paid shadowing** when audit places appear.
I would distinguish **2031 chats** from later robots.
think: I could learn **audit rules** while my current lead wage still covers our part of the mortgage.
I know another **screen role** might also shrink.
do: Keep my **paid outage shift** and request a paid audit shadow day only if a place is posted.
Complete **funded required audit training** on paid time only for posted paid work with written mortgage-covering wages/hours after travel and workable pickup.
Move after 2031 only on a **written offer** meeting those terms after comparing both household rotas.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to verify a paid route.
S3.quote: I want a paid bridge rather than a shiny title.
fieldNote: He rejects an **unposted course** as a job route.
His **shadow day** must be paid to test income.
He and Salma check **both rotas** before moving on a written offer.

steps.text: Keep leading paid outage disputes while audit places are checked
Take required funded paid-time course only for posted work with written net mortgage-covering wages/hours fitting pickup
Move on written offer with travel-adjusted mortgage-covering wages, hours and pickup after comparing both rotas
Request paid service-audit shadow day only if employer posts a place

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say a decade gives us time to build savings and see which roles pay, rather than chase every new title. General AI reaches the chats in 2036, with hands-on robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 I might still owe the mortgage, though the children should be older. I would like a full year of expenses saved before a risky job move.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep leading the outage team and save a fixed part of each pay toward a year of expenses. I will inspect posted audit roles twice a year. If my call hours fall in the first year after 2036, I will move only for a written paid offer with wages and hours covering the mortgage after travel, after Salma and I check both rotas.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about a distant change but secure enough to plan now. Ten years would make careful choices possible if we use the current wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the savings target slips?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If one of our wages falls, the year-long target moves back. I will not borrow just to make the number on a statement look good.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you tell the children to choose different work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell them to ask what a full week pays and who covers the bills if hours disappear. I would not pretend I know which jobs exist in ten years.

say: I would compare **paid roles** over the decade by their full weekly hours rather than the title alone.
I would separate **2036 chat risk** from later robots.
think: I may still owe a **mortgage at 53**, although the children should be older.
I want **one year saved** before a risky move.
do: Keep leading **outage disputes** and save from actual wages.
Move after cuts only on **written paid offer** with travel-adjusted mortgage-covering wages, hours and both rotas.
feel: **Uneasy** about later change, secure enough now.
S4.quote: I will not borrow just to make the number on a statement look good.
fieldNote: His **one-year target** moves back if either wage falls.
He compares **full-week pay** and travel costs, not attractive job titles.
A written move needs both **household rotas** to work.

steps.text: Keep leading paid outage dispute shifts
Save a fixed pay share toward one year before risky moves; delay if wages fall
Move after cuts on written paid offer covering mortgage after travel, full hours and both rotas
Inspect posted audit roles twice yearly while current lead wages continue

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. Five months saved buys some search time, but it cannot replace my wage if every nearby centre cuts. Written dates and a posted paid audit role with funded training would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who checks an outage credit after the machine closes the case. A wrong credit has a real address and a real bill. Someone needs paid time to find it.

headlineQuote: A wrong credit has a real address and a real bill.
portrait: Tomas is a **43-year-old skilled lead** with a two-year college diploma and typical pay.
He uses **approved AI daily** while checking outage logs and billing addresses.
His **five-month reserve**, mortgage, children and some nearby centres give him a limited search window.
He wants **paid audit training** and written travel-adjusted wages before a move.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his lead wage while nearby centres also cut.
whatWouldHelp: **Written dates** and posted paid audit work with funded training would help.
